cells.gaps: The share is 60 of 432 principal centres on BUNEC's figures of 14 September 2026, which the source calls a pilot phase; the 2,400 or so secondary centres are outside the denominator and are planned to stay on paper, so the share of all local offices is lower and not published. `made` disagrees: Digital Business Africa says the communes' computerised birth acts are integrated into the central SIGEC platform (CMR-089, December 2025), while UNDP's newer account has each East Region commune on its own server, transmitting statistics to BUNEC (CMR-017, August 2026); the newest stands, and neither says the entry reaches a national register at registration. Last twelve months disagree: EcoMatin says the rate has hardly moved since April 2022, while dated events show first digital birth acts at Limbe I on 7 January 2026 and in the East Region by August 2026. No national budget line is stated; one commune's maintenance line does not carry the country.
cells.note: Births are produced in the system at council centres in several regions, a minority of offices, on servers held in the commune. Not stage 4: the share is far under half, and the one fact placing the record in the central platform is older than the account of commune servers.
